dialogue.text: [warm, wry] Level one: you're fifty-nine dollars short before payday, so you lose thirty-five dollars to a bank fee. But why does that same bank pamper you at fifty million?
[warm, wry] We're going to climb seven levels of money, all the way up to fifty million in the bank, and at every level, the same bank treats you like a different person.

[warm, wry] Here's how that fee happened. Last night you filled up your tank with almost nothing in your account, because payday is on Friday. Your bank could have simply declined the card. Instead it paid, and at 7:52 this morning your phone lit up with the fee.

[warm, wry] Banks call that an overdraft. What really happened is your bank lent you fifty-nine dollars for four days and charged you thirty-five for it. If that were a normal loan, it would be over five thousand percent interest a year. And the strangest part is that you agreed to it. You just don't remember when.

[warm, wry] Now meet Jess. She did the exact same thing last night: same gas station, same fee. She's sitting in her car, doing the math on rent, and then she walks inside to start her shift, because she works at that bank. It's her first week as a teller.

[warm, wry] That's Gloria, thirty years at this counter. Today Jess will watch customers from every level come to her window, and by five o'clock she'll know who's paying for all the pampering at the top. It might be you. She'll also find a setting on your phone that the bank really hopes you never touch.
